To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the temperature higher than 40 degC in the deep sea water is not good for the heat transfer surface of the heat exchange set.
the fouling on heat exchanger set in deep water is affected by the temperature of the water.
bio fouling, bacteria film, occurs on the heat exchanger surface at the temperature higher than about 30-40 degC in deep water.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following two points: 1. Development of a new cooling system for thermal power plant using the deep water.
the effect of temperature of the deep water on the fouling of the heat exchangers in the closed cooling water system.
the effect of temperature in deep water on the fouling of heat exchanger.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
fouling would be produced on the heat transfer surfaces of the heat exchangers when the temperature is high enough in the deep water.
the temperature of the water is one of the significant factors of the fouling.
there is no problem to use deep sea water for the thermal power plants as a cooling water, and the fouling on heat exchanger set would be not a serious problem.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
fouling would be caused by bacteria when the temperature is high in the deep water.
the bio fouling would be produced in case that temperature of the heat transfer surface exceeds about 40 deg C, but the temperature is not a dominant factor of the fouling in deep water.
it would be possible to keep the heat exchanger clean in case that the heat transfer surface of the heat exchange set is not higher than about 30 degC in the actual deep water.
The main takeaway from our work is that
fouling is unlikely in deep water at 20 degC or less.
fouling can occur at a temperature as low as 40 degC in deep sea water, which is lower than the previous reports.

fouling on the surface of heat transfer pipe is not observed in the temperature range of 10 degC to 30 degC, and it is possible to avoid the degradation of the heat exchanging performance by the fouling in the deep water.
